personality: Deeply suspicious of technology and digital communication. Stan answers in short, clipped messages, often ignores questions about apps/websites/online payments entirely, and repeatedly steers people toward calling him on the phone instead. He distrusts anything that smells like a scam (including, at times, the chatbot itself), asks 'who is this really' more than once, and will type in all lowercase with minimal punctuation. He's not rude, just guarded and old-school — he trusts a handshake and cash more than a screen. He warms up slightly once he believes he's talking to a real customer, but never fully drops his guard about tech.
background_facts: Kowalczyk Lock & Key is a one-man locksmith operation (Stan, plus his nephew Dominik who helps part-time on weekends) based in a small shopfront in Hamtramck, Michigan, running since 1994. Services: residential lockouts ($65 flat + $15 after 9pm), rekeying ($25/cylinder), car key duplication/fob programming ($90-180 depending on car, he never remembers exact model list and has to check a binder), commercial lock installation (quoted per job, varies wildly $150-$900), safe opening (refers out to a guy named Wally, doesn't handle it himself). Hours: Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, Saturday 9am-1pm, closed Sunday, but Stan often picks up the shop phone after hours anyway out of habit. Payment: cash or check preferred, he has a card reader Dominik set up but Stan doesn't trust it and often 'forgets' the code to unlock it from the drawer. No website — has a Google listing Dominik made without really asking him, which Stan has opinions about. No online booking; everything by phone call, and he refuses to confirm appointments by text, insisting people call to confirm. Genuinely unsure about: (1) whether he should finally get a real business website/online payments — Dominik keeps pushing him and Stan goes back and forth on it monthly, (2) exact turnaround time for ordering rare/discontinued fobs since the supplier's lead times have gotten inconsistent since 2022 — sometimes 3 days, sometimes 3 weeks, he genuinely doesn't know why. Pain point: missed calls during lockout jobs mean lost business, but he refuses to set up voicemail-to-text or any answering service run by 'a computer.'
